description: Scenario-keyed sabotage matrix for the required-tools preflight. Each scenario names one deliberately induced proxy state and the EXACT per-tool verdict it must produce: status, reason, retryable and action (an omitted action means the reason carries none). The set-level verdict and CLI exit code are the ones a single-tool request of that shape must report. internal/server/preflight_e2e_test.go drives every scenario against a real mcpproxy binary and asserts these values independently, and a reflection check fails if any code of the 15-code enum has no scenario here.

surfaces.e2e: induced against a running mcpproxy binary with sabotaged fixture upstreams
surfaces.state-injected: induced by injecting the connection-state snapshot the runtime cannot be forced into deterministically from outside

scenarios.sabotage: none: indexed, approved tool on an enabled, healthy, trusted server — asserted both unfiltered and under each of the three annotation filters, since a fully annotated tool must survive all of them
POST /api/v1/servers/{server}/quarantine on a previously healthy, indexed server
rewrite the upstream tool's description in the fixture tools file, then restart the server so the proxy re-lists it (rug-pull guard trips)
add a tool to the fixture tools file after the trusted server's baseline was auto-approved, then restart the server
POST /api/v1/servers/{server}/tools/block for one tool
server configured with disabled_tools containing the requested tool
server configured with enabled:false
arm the fixture's fail-switch file, SIGKILL the upstream process, then force a reconnect: the restarted fixture exits immediately, so the server settles in a stable non-connected state

restart an already-indexed server with a long initialize delay, so it sits in connecting/discovering while its tools remain in the shared index (a never-indexed server would report not_found instead: existence outranks connection state)
policy.read_only_only against a tool whose upstream definition declares no annotations
policy.exclude_destructive against a tool with no destructiveHint and no read-only hint
policy.exclude_open_world against a tool with no openWorldHint
policy.read_only_only against a tool explicitly annotated readOnlyHint:false
policy.exclude_destructive against a tool explicitly annotated destructiveHint:true
policy.exclude_open_world against a tool explicitly annotated openWorldHint:true
misspelled tool name on a configured, healthy server
tool id naming a server that is not configured at all
pin_hash at the current schema version whose digest does not match the tool's stored hash
pin_hash carrying the tool's CURRENT digest under a different hash schema version (simulates a proxy-side hash-algorithm bump)
connection-state snapshot reports the deferred-OAuth PendingAuth state for the server
preflight under a profile whose server list excludes the requested tool's server, called with the operator API key

same out-of-scope request as profile_out_of_scope_operator, called with an agent token whose allowed_servers excludes the server: scope-silence maps it to a plain not_found, byte-indistinguishable from an absent tool
